nodes.label: Fingerprint name-versus-shape agreement
nodes.summary: Reused id. Finding F1 on PR #440: GROUP_COLUMNS does double duty as the fingerprint expectation and as the source `snipset init` builds CREATE TABLE from, so adding a column name to the constant without a matching arm in column_definition satisfies the name check and silently produces the wrong type.

nodes.label: column_definition catch-all arm
nodes.summary: Reused id. init.rs has no `research_tag` arm, so `_ => format!("{column} TEXT")` creates it as nullable TEXT. Measured against the 209 MB production database: five of twelve groups columns and seven of twenty-six snippets columns diverge from what the app declares, four of the eight predating PR #440.

nodes.label: SQLite TEXT affinity breaks the rusqlite integer read
nodes.norm_label: sqlite text affinity breaks the rusqlite integer read
nodes.summary: The measured chain behind F1: a column created as TEXT has TEXT affinity, which converts the desktop's integer 1 into '1' on write; rusqlite 0.40.2 ValueRef::as_i64 matches only ValueRef::Integer, read from the vendored crate at the locked version, so the integer read fails; `research_tagged_group_uuids` and `get_all_groups` then disagree on the same row. The wrong type is permanent because the desktop's has_col guard skips the migration.

nodes.label: has_col guard makes the migration array a no-op, so schema.rs is the authority
nodes.norm_label: has col guard makes the migration array a no op so schema rs is the authority
nodes.summary: The parity test's disagreement branch fired on ten columns and the measurement said the migration array, not schema.rs, is the wrong source of truth: those ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements are wrapped in a has_col guard, so on any database that already has the column they do nothing. Six columns measured notnull=0 on the real database, including is_deleted.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - super-ultra-code-plan-pr-delivery-session [ses_f08d01cd8ffe92DE7Adnn8J1o5].md:L11511] The desktop app's six-column NOT NULL migration defect is recorded and deferred, not fixed, because editing the app's upgrade path for real user databases needs its own approval

nodes.label: The guard test reads the app's migration source instead of restating the column list
nodes.norm_label: the guard test reads the app's migration source instead of restating the column list
nodes.summary: Reused id. Chunk K4 wrote `init_column_shapes_match_what_the_desktop_app_declares`, a source-derived parity test with no hardcoded expectations: it parses schema.rs and the migration arrays, compares them column by column, and against the live table the CLI created. RED at exit 100 with 12 named divergences, then 188 green.

nodes.label: match arm order silently overrides a column default
nodes.norm_label: match arm order silently overrides a column default
nodes.summary: `enabled` shared an or-pattern arm emitting INTEGER DEFAULT 0 with seven other columns while the app declares DEFAULT 1, so a group inserted without an explicit enabled came out disabled in a CLI-created database. match takes the first arm that matches, so merging `enabled` back into the shared pattern reinstates the bug without a compile error.

nodes.label: A negative control stays green when the mutation premise no longer holds
nodes.norm_label: a negative control stays green when the mutation premise no longer holds
nodes.summary: A claimed negative control B moved the `enabled` arm below the shared arm and the test stayed green. The control was invalid: the arm had already been split out by a sibling chunk, so there was no ordering constraint left to test. The valid control merges `enabled` back into the or-pattern, and that does go red.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent-compiler policy
nodes.summary: Reused id. The K4 parity test shipped with three defects only compilation exposed: a format string referencing two bindings that did not exist, and a use of nightly-only str_as_str. That is the stated reason the repo keeps every compiler operation in the parent, and why the parent's RED capture on vps-bcb was the gate.

nodes.label: Another session live on the PR branch forces a fresh branch off main
nodes.norm_label: another session live on the pr branch forces a fresh branch off main
nodes.summary: The main checkout carried three unpushed commits and a dirty file from another session on fix/cli-schema-fingerprint-research-tag. The follow-up work went to a worktree beside the repo on pr440/followups, and when PR #440 was merged by someone else before the commits reached it, the work branched fresh off main and was cherry-picked so #442 carried only this work. The push was a plain fast-forward, never a force.

nodes.label: Clippy clean is not rustfmt clean
nodes.norm_label: clippy clean is not rustfmt clean
nodes.summary: A self-correction inside the review: clippy 0 warnings and 0 errors had been reported as a complete verification, but cargo fmt --check was never run. The PR head 2ff5df447 had three rustfmt violations in fingerprint_test.rs at lines 68, 114 and 121. The repository's ci:rust:lint gate includes rustfmt, so this would have been caught in CI had the workflow triggers not been disabled.

nodes.label: pr-registry.mjs tracks ai-skills sessions, not Snipset pull requests
nodes.norm_label: pr registry mjs tracks ai skills sessions not snipset pull requests
nodes.summary: PR #440 was never claimed through pr-registry.mjs because it predates the registry and its branch is not a derived ai/<plan>/<session> name, so it is invisible to the computed merge order. Same for #442 and the dependabot PRs. Flagged as a real gap for batch merging over this repository, and left unfixed because claiming a divergent branch would break one-PR-per-session.

nodes.label: Post-merge re-verification on the new base
nodes.norm_label: post merge re verification on the new base
nodes.summary: After #442 merged as 30deffa54, the suite was re-run on vps-bcb after git pull --ff-only onto that commit rather than re-reading the pre-merge result: 188 passed, clippy 0, fmt clean. An empty diff against the verified branch proved main content byte-identical, because the merge rebased and SHA ancestry could not.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - super-ultra-code-plan-pr-delivery-session [ses_f08d01cd8ffe92DE7Adnn8J1o5].md:L17460] The post-merge run is the evidence for *this* merge, not a re-read of the pre-merge one.

nodes.label: Each schema mismatch direction has its own remedy
nodes.norm_label: each schema mismatch direction has its own remedy
nodes.summary: The shipped guide documented only `unexpected columns` and told users to rebuild the CLI from the app's revision, which is not the fix for a missing column, since a CLI built from the app's revision expects the same absent column. Missing columns means open the app once or run `snipset init --force`, which renames the old file to a timestamped backup and never deletes it.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - super-ultra-code-plan-pr-delivery-session [ses_f08d01cd8ffe92DE7Adnn8J1o5].md:L09001] K3's blast-radius answer changes where the hint goes: `DbError::Schema` is an overloaded variant used at **41 sites**, so the hint must go in `assert_schema` (`db/mod.rs:97`), not in the `Display` arm at `:41` and not in `SchemaDiff::message()`, which `doctor` publishes as a machine-readable `detail` field.

nodes.label: Sidecar rebuild signal when the app schema changes
nodes.norm_label: sidecar rebuild signal when the app schema changes
nodes.summary: Root cause of the incident class: snipset-cli is versioned 0.2.0 independently of the app, so nothing signals a sidecar rebuild when the app schema changes. Research verified no user_version or schema_revision exists anywhere and no macOS target or build script exists. Kept as a Draft plan because it proposes making a stale sidecar a fatal build failure.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - super-ultra-code-plan-pr-delivery-session [ses_f08d01cd8ffe92DE7Adnn8J1o5].md:L17252] The plan at `docs/code-plan/plans/2026-10-01-sidecar-rebuild-signal.md` is **Draft and unapproved**, deliberately: it proposes making a stale sidecar a fatal build failure, which overrides a deliberate decision documented at `stage-cli-sidecar.mjs:4-6`.
